minutes.headline: Select Board heard town counsel say the Conservation Commission may ban firearms on its land; no vote taken on it.
minutes.summary: The board heard town counsel's opinion on firearms possession and hunting on town and conservation land, with conservation commission members present. Board members questioned the legal basis, enforcement and liability, and the commission is revising its rules. The town manager also reported on COVID, a health insurance premium holiday, and a library/TCP building cost estimate. The board approved minutes and went into executive session.

what_happened.line: Town counsel gave the Select Board an opinion on firearms and hunting on town and conservation land; no vote was taken on it.
Board members questioned the legal basis, enforcement and liability of a ban, and the Conservation Commission is revising its land use rules.
The Conservation Commission will send its latest land use regulations to the board and post them before the February 17 public hearing.
The town manager reported a one-month health insurance premium holiday next fiscal year, covering school and town active plans and retirees.
The architect's estimate for the TCP building came in far higher once contingency and escalation were added.

why_it_matters: Rules on firearms and hunting on conservation land would change how residents can use town-owned open space, and the commission's regulations are set at a public hearing.
The premium holiday and the higher TCP building estimate both bear on next year's town and school budgets, and so on tax bills.
watch_next: February 17 public hearing on the Conservation Commission's land use regulations.
The full Hunting Hills conservation restriction, to be forwarded to the board, and the February 16 workshop on appointments.
